title.en: Why oxygen is not simply O

text.en: The air we breathe contains oxygen, but there is no single free oxygen atom floating about; atoms of oxygen join in pairs. Most elements prefer to exist in combination, and this leads us to molecules.

Except noble gases, atoms of most elements exist in combined form; a molecule is a combination of two or more atoms held together by strong chemical bonds.
All compounds are molecules, but all molecules are not compounds, because a molecule can also be made of atoms of the same element.
A molecule made of similar atoms is homoatomic, like O2 and O3, and one made of different atoms in a fixed ratio is heteroatomic, like HCl and H2O.
The number of atoms in a molecule is its atomicity; one atom is monoatomic, two is diatomic, three is triatomic and more than three is polyatomic.
Hydrogen, nitrogen and the halogens exist as diatomic molecules, while phosphorus P4 and sulphur S8 are polyatomic.
The atomic mass of an element is the average of the masses of its isotopes weighted by their abundance; for boron, 20 percent of B-10 and 80 percent of B-11 gives 10.8 amu.
The relative molecular mass is the ratio of the mass of one molecule to one twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom, so it has no unit.
It is found by adding the relative atomic masses of all the atoms in the molecule, so water is 2 x 1 + 16 = 18 and carbon dioxide is 12 + 32 = 44.
When the molecular mass is expressed in grams it is called the gram molecular mass, for example 18 g for water and 36.5 g for HCl.
The percentage composition of an element in a compound is (mass of that element in one formula unit divided by the molecular mass) times 100.

problem.en: Find the relative molecular mass of H2SO4 (H = 1, S = 32, O = 16) and the percentage of oxygen in it.

text.en: H2SO4 has 2 hydrogen, 1 sulphur and 4 oxygen atoms.

prompt.en: Classify O2, O3, HCl, H2O and P4 by atomicity and by kind of atoms.

points.en: Atomicity is the number of atoms in a molecule.
RMM = sum of relative atomic masses (no unit); gram molecular mass is in grams.
Average atomic mass = sum of (isotope mass x abundance).
% of element = (mass of element / RMM) x 100.
